welcome_page.title: Cycling – Your trips and road safety
welcome_page.description:
A few questions about getting around by bike or e-bike, including shared bikes. If you rarely cycle, we only ask why.

Taking part is voluntary and you can skip any question. Your answers are not linked to your name, and no public authority receives them.

Learn more about SmartUrbanity

Only the SmartUrbanity research team reads your answers. We keep them for research for 36 months; then we delete them or make them anonymous.

questions.text: Do you ride a bike or e-bike to get around at least once a week?
questions.help: Your own bike or a shared one. Rides just for sport count too.

options.text: Yes
No

questions.text: Why do you rarely cycle? (Select all that apply)

options.text: I don't have a bike or e-bike I can use
The places I go are too far or cycling takes too long
Cycling is tiring or physically difficult for me
I feel unsafe cycling (traffic, crime or harassment)
There are no good cycle lanes or safe places to leave a bike
Another reason

options.text: My own bike

A shared bike
A shared e-bike

questions.text: How confident do you feel cycling in city traffic?

options.text: Not at all: I avoid cycling in traffic
Not very: I cycle in traffic only when I have to
In between

questions.text: Does cycling in your daily life help your health or your mood?

options.text: Yes
No

questions.text: In the same trip, do you usually combine cycling with another way of travelling?
questions.help: For example bike and train, or car and metro. A short walk to a stop or to a parked vehicle does not count.

options.text: Yes
No

questions.text: Which other ways of travelling do you use in the same trip? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Walking (as the main mode for most of the trip, not short access or transfer walking)
Car
Car sharing
Motorcycle, scooter or moped
Bus
Tram
Metro
Regional or suburban train
e-scooter (private)
e-scooter (shared)

questions.text: What difficulties do you experience when combining different transport modes (e.g. bike + public transport, car + metro, walking + bus)?

options.text: Vehicles are too crowded (e.g. no space for a bicycle or luggage)
Poor coordination between modes (long waiting times, missed connections)
Lack of infrastructure (e.g. no bicycle parking or no bicycle access on public transport)
Complicated transfers (stations far apart, unclear routes)
Travel time becomes too long
Cost is too high when combining modes
Safety concerns (traffic, theft, unsafe areas)
Services are infrequent or do not run in the evening
Lack of reliable information (schedules, delays)
Physical effort is too high (e.g. carrying a bicycle or walking long distances)
Accessibility issues (stairs, no elevators, etc.)
Weather-related difficulties
I do not experience significant difficulties

questions.text: When you face these difficulties, how do you mostly respond?

options.text: I stop using one of the modes (e.g. stop bringing my bike)
I switch to a single mode (e.g. only car, only public transport)
I change the time of travel (e.g. avoid peak hours)
I change the route or transfer point
I choose a different combination of modes
I continue using the same combination despite difficulties
I reduce how often I make that trip
I look for alternative solutions (e.g. bike sharing instead of own bike)
I avoid that trip entirely if possible
I do not experience significant difficulties

questions.text: When you cycle, how quick are your reflexes if something happens suddenly?
questions.help: Think about how quickly you can react, for example when a car door opens suddenly.

options.text: Not quick at all: I often cannot react in time
A little quick: sometimes I react late
Fairly quick: I usually react in time
Very quick: I almost always react in time
Extremely quick: I always react in time

questions.text: How good are the cycle lanes and paths on your usual route?
questions.help: Think of cycle lanes, cycle paths and their signs and markings.

options.text: There are none, or almost none
There are some, but they stop and start or are badly made
They cover part of my route
They are good on most of my route
They are very good all along my route

questions.text: What gets in your way on your usual bike route?

options.text: Potholes, bumps or cobblestones
Steep or sudden slopes
Cars or vans parked in the cycle lane
People on foot or e-scooters in the cycle lane
Bins, signs or boards in the cycle path
A cycle path or lane that ends abruptly
No crossings or traffic lights for bikes
Badly designed junctions or roundabouts
Tram tracks
Edges of the sharing area, so I cannot leave the vehicle where I arrive
Stairs or steps on the route with no ramp or wheel channel
Nothing gets in my way

questions.text: When the road surface is bad, what do you do on the bike?
questions.help: For example potholes, cobblestones or uneven ground.

options.text: It doesn't affect me
I notice it, but I don't change anything
I slow down or ride around it, on the same route
I take other roads, even if they are longer
It limits where and how often I can cycle

questions.text: Does heavy or fast traffic on your route change how you cycle?

options.text: No, traffic doesn't bother me
I notice it, but it rarely changes my comfort or route
It sometimes makes cycling less pleasant
It often makes me feel stressed or unsafe
I change my route or time to avoid it

options.text: Car drivers

Bus drivers
Delivery vehicles (vans, cargo bikes, scooters)

Other cyclists
E-scooter riders
Pedestrians
Nobody in particular

options.text: Poor visibility or limited sightlines
Unsafe behaviour from drivers, riders or pedestrians
Crowding
Conflicts with other road users
